title: Nested patterns arise from rules that emulate themselves

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Nested patterns arise from rules that emulate themselves

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: A cellular automaton whose blocks of cells evolve by the same rule as individual cells must produce patterns that are either essentially uniform or nested; this self-emulation is why rule 90 and rules that emulate it produce nested patterns.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And this can be achieved in only two ways: either the pattern must be essentially uniform, or it must have a nested structure—just like we see in rule 90.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 6, “Starting from Randomness”; section “Special Initial Conditions” (from p. 266), p. 271. Scope: self-emulating cellular automata

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch06-19: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Specific self-emulation identities and rule 90's nested form are exactly checkable. The asserted dichotomy needs formal qualifications and is doubtful over the full stated scope, so only the intended restricted version is resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Formalize self-emulation as a block map commuting with the cellular-automaton evolution, then prove that repeated rescaling constrains configurations to uniform or self-similar nested forms under the intended assumptions. Search finite rule and block spaces for a self-emulating counterexample with another morphology.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Self-simulation can support complex behavior in broader automaton classes.

The claim omits assumptions on the block map and initial condition.

“Nested” lacks a single formal definition.

fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.7
data existence: 0.92
operationalizability: 0.75
data adequacy: 0.65
discriminating power: 0.82

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Exact self-emulation means the spacetime diagram is unchanged by a fixed rescaling, and the configurations with that invariance are the uniform and the hierarchically nested ones. That is a short structural proof once the blocking is formalized, and rule 90 supplies a fully checkable instance. The argument covers the conditional scope the sentence actually states.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Assume a blocking under which blocks obey the same rule as cells, and require the spacetime diagram to equal its own rescaling. The configurations invariant under that rescaling are the uniform and the nested ones; a self-emulating rule with a spacetime diagram outside those two forms would refute the dichotomy.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The dichotomy covers exact self-emulation, not a merely similar picture.

Nested has to mean invariance under the same blocking the rule emulates.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.85
discriminating power: 0.82
analysis feasibility: 0.78
data adequacy: 0.88
operationalizability: 0.82
